headline: River Permits and High Alpine Access Guidelines
reservation: Commercial rafting requires booking through licensed outfitters, while private river users must adhere to Arkansas Headwaters Recreation Area (AHRA) rules. Camping in the Collegiate Peaks wilderness requires self-registration; always check the latest US Forest Service guidelines for seasonal fire bans.

days.title: Arkansas River Whitewater
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Downtown Buena Vista

stops.name: Browns Canyon National Monument
stops.detail: Experience a guided rafting trip through the granite canyons of this federally protected waterway.

stops.name: Buena Vista River Park
stops.detail: Watch expert kayakers navigate the whitewater park features from the shore paths.

days.driving: Walking distance for town sites; allow 30 minutes for outfitter shuttles.
days.note: River flows peak in June; check with outfitters for age and skill requirements.

days.title: Collegiate Peaks High Country
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Cottonwood Creek Trailhead

stops.name: Cottonwood Pass
stops.detail: Drive to the Continental Divide at 12,126 feet for panoramic views of the Sawatch Range.

stops.name: Mount Princeton Overlook
stops.detail: View the iconic 14,000-foot peak from the valley floor or lower forest roads.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the mountain pass drive; conditions vary significantly with weather.
days.note: The pass is seasonally closed in winter; check CDOT for opening dates.

days.title: Valley Relaxation and History

stops.name: St. Elmo Ghost Town
stops.detail: Visit one of Colorado's best-preserved mining towns, located a short drive west of the valley.

stops.name: Chaffee County Heritage Area
stops.detail: Explore the agricultural roots of the Upper Arkansas Valley along the riverside.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the round trip to St. Elmo; road is unpaved but generally graded.
days.note: Respect private property boundaries in the ghost town areas.

intel.title: Trailhead Saturation
intel.text: Popular trailheads for the Collegiate Peaks fill before 7 AM on summer weekends. Have a secondary lower-elevation plan in case the primary lot is full.

intel.title: Mountain Topography
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable in town but vanishes once you enter the canyons or ascend Cottonwood Pass. Off-line navigation is essential for backcountry exploration.

intel.title: Valley Services
intel.text: Buena Vista is the primary hub for fuel and groceries in the upper valley. Supplies are extremely limited once you head west toward the Continental Divide.

intel.title: Afternoon Lightning
intel.text: Mountain storms typically develop by 1 PM during July and August. Plan to be off high ridges and summits by noon to ensure safety.

intel.title: River Access Points
intel.text: Public access to the Arkansas River is restricted to designated AHRA sites. Ensure you are launching and landing at official points to respect private land.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at EGE or Denver, stop in Silverthorne or Fairplay for supplies, and settle into your valley lodging before the sun sets behind the peaks.
plan.vehicle: An AWD vehicle is recommended for reaching higher trailheads, though town and the pass road are paved.
plan.goldenHour: Cottonwood Pass provides an expansive western horizon for sunset; bring warm layers for the high-altitude chill.
